external_prior_art.title: Evaluating the Relevance of Uncertainty Estimators for LLM Hallucination

external_claim_level_prior_art.title: Think Through Uncertainty: Improving Long-Form Generation Factuality via Reasoning Calibration

observation: External evidence reports that the association between uncertainty estimators and hallucination is highly variable across hallucination types and models. Separate external work proposes claim-level confidence and selective abstention for long-form factuality. Neither result is Memorithm evidence; both motivate bounded, stratified ablations under a frozen protocol.

hypothesis.statement: No candidate uncertainty estimator will be treated as a universal hallucination proxy; predictive utility must be demonstrated separately within each preregistered model x task x hallucination-type stratum.
hypothesis.falsification: The hypothesis is provisionally falsified for the authorized Development/Validation population only if a preregistered estimator shows materially stable predictive utility across every preregistered stratum under the frozen acceptance rule.

claim_level_secondary_hypothesis.statement: Within each frozen stratum, claim-level uncertainty with selective abstention will be compared against response-level uncertainty and no-abstention calibration under matched authorized populations and declared compute; superiority is not assumed.
claim_level_secondary_hypothesis.falsification: Record a negative or inconclusive result if the frozen claim-level arm fails its preregistered risk-coverage and calibration materiality rules, or if any apparent gain is accompanied by an unacceptable loss in coverage, useful-task performance, or retention of originally correct answers. Validation results may not trigger retuning.
